Article Title: 'Foreigners wondering what is this India': Pranesh on GCL, Praggnanandhaa 'rumours', and Vaishali | Exclusive
Article Text:
Vaishali's mother Nagalakshmi, Pranesh M, Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa, and Vaibhav Suri (Photo by Michal Walusza)

From an 1800-rated player to Vaishali’s trusted confidant

Young Pranesh with his coach RB Ramesh (Special Arrangements)

Will Pranesh join Vaishali for her Women's World Championship match?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: Bengaluru's Lalit Ashok hotel, where season 4 of the Global Chess League (GCL) is unfolding, has not been short on marquee pairings this week, but the one that turned heads on Monday belonged to a 20-year-old who wasn't even supposed to be here. Chennai-born Grandmaster Pranesh M walked into this year's tournament as a late replacement for Vladimir Fedoseev, slotted onto Mumba Masters' board two, and has spent the tournament making that footnote look increasingly irrelevant, first by beating Anish Giri on the opening day, then, more strikingly, by dismantling Levon Aronian's position from the white side of a Sicilian, punishing an over-optimistic kingside pawn push with the kind of clean, calculated finish that has become his signature."I think in the opening I kind of outplayed him (Levon)," Pranesh told TimesofIndia.com during an exclusive conversation on the sidelines of the GCL. "He went for g5, slightly a mistake, but I don't know what else he could have done. It just looked so bad for him. I had clear plans, and it's hard to play faster than one moves."Board 2, he says, hasn't intimidated him the way some might expect from a teenager thrown in among a field this strong."I'm just feeling really happy. I think I can actually compete with them," he added with a smile.In August, just before joining his GCL side, Pranesh won the Kanizsa Open in Hungary outright, going unbeaten across nine rounds to push his rating into the world's top 50.It capped a stretch that began, less visibly, in Cyprus, where he spent weeks not playing for himself at all, but working as GM Vaishali Rameshbabu's second and training partner through her run to the Women's Candidates title.Vaishali and her coach RB Ramesh have been candid about why Pranesh was brought into that camp in the first place. Vaishali, for all her poker-faced reputation at the board, takes losses hard, and Ramesh and his wife Aarthie wanted someone around who could keep the mood light. Pranesh's own account of the job is characteristically low-key, though."Mainly Vaishali akka gets really serious during the game, and after the game she'll be wondering where she made a mistake," Pranesh revealed. "I'll just tell her, don't care; even if you don't blunder, you'll win the tournament. There were a lot of blunders in that tournament, so. I was just being myself."During the Candidates, he was around Vaishali; in the broader Chess Gurukul ecosystem, he grew up alongside players such as Praggnanandhaa and Aravindh Chithambaram. His relationship with Vaishali goes back years, to a time when he was rated nowhere near where he is now.“I went with Vaishali because I have known her for a long time,” he said. “Even when I was like 1800, she was still going with Ramesh sir.”Was there any particular trick the youngster used to keep her calm? he replied with a chuckle, "It (the tendency to be funny around close ones) is natural now. I think from a young age, I kind of developed it. I don't know. I was just being myself."It wasn't only Vaishali's tournament that mattered to him that fortnight. Her brother, Praggnanandhaa, entered the men's Candidates as India's only hope before finishing second-last in the standings. The margin between the two campaigns is not lost on anyone who follows Indian chess closely.Pranesh, asked directly whether the mood inside the camp shifted after Pragg's result, waved off any suggestion of tension, adding, "It's just normal. There's nothing different between the performance and everything."He was equally quick to shut down reports that he'd been formally part of Pragg's team as well. "Not really, it's just rumours. I was just part of Vaishali's team. But I was talking with both of them," he remarked.That mix of steadiness and self-deprecation runs through most of how Pranesh talks about this year. He credits a recent training block under Ramesh, alongside the likes of R Praggnanandhaa and Aravindh Chithambaram.“The purpose was to make us stronger,” Pranesh, who is now rated 2674 and aiming to cross 2700, said. “Each class will be really some difficult puzzles and some interesting puzzles also, to make some decisions and everything.”As far as his time in Bengaluru so far is concerned, the GCL bubble itself has clearly left an impression, mostly for reasons that have nothing to do with chess. He described the phenomenon of Indian crowds chanting for players as something that visibly rattles foreign competitors."The foreigners are just wondering what is this India," he said, recalling a conversation with his own American teammate, GM Carissa Yip. "She told me she's never seen something like this in the US.“Every strong player is coming and playing here, and even Magnus (Carlsen) is playing here. That is a big achievement.”Also Read: Pranesh M, son of anganwadi worker, is India's top chess grandmaster And, lastly, when asked about the chances of him joining Vaishali for her upcoming Women's World Championship match, he couldn't stop laughing before murmuring, “Maybe, but I don’t know. First of all, I don't know when the dates will be released.”
Article Summary: Chennai-born Grandmaster Pranesh M walked into this year's tournament as a late replacement for Vladimir Fedoseev, slotted onto Mumba Masters' board two. He has spent the tournament making that footnote look increasingly irrelevant, first by beating Anish Giri on the opening day.

Article Title: In 2018, Vidarsa K Vinod walked into a college NCC trial simply to experience holding a rifle; eight years, borrowed equipment and a family loan later, she is going to the Asian Games
Article Text:
Vidarsa K Vinod is set to make her Asian Games debut at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games in Japan

She entered shooting almost by chance

Vidarsa K Vinod’s family took a loan in 2021 to help her buy her first rifle, a crucial step in her journey towards international shooting.

A question changed her career

From Kerala to Delhi

Coach Manoj Kumar helped her adapt to a lighter rifle that she now uses in competition.

A rifle that was never meant to be hers

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

From her first international medal to the Asian Games

When Vidarsa K Vinod walked into an NCC shooting trial at her college in Kozhikode in 2018, she wanted to experience what it felt like to hold a rifle. Eight years later, that casual decision has taken the Kerala shooter to the biggest stage of her career. Vinod is set to make her Asian Games debut in Aichi-Nagoya, representing India in the women’s 10m air rifle and 50m rifle 3 positions events.Her journey, however, was anything but straightforward. For years, she trained without owning the equipment needed to compete seriously. She relied on NCC and borrowed rifles, dealt with the financial demands of shooting and even came close to quitting before finally breaking through.According to The Indian Express, Vinod had no formal shooting training when she appeared for the NCC trial in 2018. She performed well enough to make the NCC team and soon progressed to the Kerala state team. A year later, she became the aggregate champion at the Kerala State Shooting Championship. But becoming a serious shooter required something she did not have: her own rifle.Competitive shooting is an expensive sport, with the cost of a rifle coming before expenses such as jackets and ammunition.For Vinod, that financial barrier remained a constant problem. The Covid-19 pandemic made matters worse, bringing her training to a halt.For nearly a year, she stayed away from the range and practised yoga and exercises at home. Even before that, she had been relying on borrowed or NCC equipment. Yet despite not owning a rifle, she rose to No. 1 in Kerala, according to The Indian Express.The turning point came through another shooter, Manu S Ravi, who later became her husband. After the pandemic, he asked her a simple question: why did she not own a rifle? For Vinod, the answer was obvious- she could not afford one.But the question forced her to reconsider how seriously she wanted to pursue shooting. According to India Today, Vinod discussed the matter with her parents, and in 2021 her family took a loan to buy her first rifle.The investment eventually began to pay off. With Manu’s encouragement and training under coach Manoj Kumar, her performances improved and she won her first national medal in 2022.Vinod moved to New Delhi to train at the Dr Karni Singh Shooting Range, entering a more demanding training environment. It meant living alone in an unfamiliar city while managing cooking, household responsibilities and intensive training sessions.In early 2024, after a series of near-misses and mounting financial strain, Vinod came close to walking away from shooting. She felt that her family, husband and coach had already sacrificed too much for her career. But they continued to back her, even when she had begun to doubt herself.There was another unusual twist in her equipment story. Vinod was struggling with the weight of her rifle, and coach Manoj Kumar suggested that she try a lighter model he had imported for his daughter. As per reports, Kumar's daughter ultimately chose to focus on studies, so he allowed Vinod to test the rifle.She initially refused because the rifle had been bought for his daughter. After trying it for a few days, however, Kumar told her to keep it. That lightweight rifle is now the one Vinod will carry into the Asian Games.Kumar told The Indian Express that Vinod was quick to learn and willing to accept the technical changes he introduced. Their association has continued for several years and has become an important part of her development as a shooter.The breakthrough at the international level came in 2025. Vinod represented India at the Asian Shooting Championships in Kazakhstan and won a silver medal in the team event, according to The Times of India. Since then, she has competed at three ISSF World Cups, two Asian Championships and a World Championship. She also finished sixth at a recent World Cup. Her maiden international medal at the 2025 Asian Shooting Championship helped pave the way for her selection for the Asian Games squad.Now, the woman who once borrowed rifles to continue competing is preparing to take aim for India at the Asian Games. But Vinod is not setting herself a medal target. Speaking to The Times of India, she said her coach's advice has been to focus on experiencing and learning rather than chasing the podium. The emphasis, she said, is on preparing for a longer period rather than treating the Asian Games as a single defining competition. In 2018, she had walked into an NCC trial simply to hold a rifle. Today, that rifle has taken her all the way to the Asian Games.
Article Summary: Vidarsa K Vinod is set to make her Asian Games debut at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games in Japan. For years, she trained without owning the equipment needed to compete seriously. She relied on NCC and borrowed rifles, dealt with the financial demands of shooting and even came close to quitting before finally breaking through.

Article Title: After CWG bronze, Seema Kaliramna sets sights on another step towards Olympics at Asian Games
Article Text:
Seema Kaliramna (Image credit: Special arrangement)

Seema Kaliramna (Image credit: Special arrangement)

From 54-55m in training to 59.73m

Seema Kaliramna (Image credit: Special arrangement)

The support behind Seema's comeback

Rudra will watch from home again

Seema Kaliramna and son Rudra (Image credit: Special arrangement)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The 57.44m throw in Bhubaneswar last month did not quite match the 59.73m that Seema Kaliramna had produced two months earlier. Nor did she seem particularly bothered by it.The Bhubaneswar competition was the World Athletics Silver Level Continental Tour meet at Kalinga Stadium on August 22, her first competition after the Commonwealth Games bronze in Glasgow.In the women's discus, Commonwealth Games champion Samantha Hall was in the field along with Thailand's Subenrat Insaeng and Brazil's Andressa de Morais. De Morais won with 58.66m, Hall threw 58.43m, Subenrat 58.33m, and Seema finished fourth with 57.44m.Her personal best had come at the National Inter-State Championships in June earlier this year, where she also crossed the Asian Games qualifying mark of 55.48m. A month later in Glasgow, she won Commonwealth Games bronze with 58.65m.Now, with the Asian Games approaching, the 27-year-old discus thrower is not putting a target distance on what comes next.“I just want to throw the discus as far as I can. Now, it can be 60, it can be 65, it can be 70 metres, sir. Now, whether I get the medal or not, that's another story, sir. I just want to do my best, sir,” Seema told Timesofindia.com in an exclusive interaction ahead of the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, which begin on September 19.The 60m mark is still to come in competition, but Seema is in no hurry to force it, in fact, she laughs off the temptation to chase it too quickly.“It's better if we progress slowly. If we progress completely, it gets a little messy.”Her coach and husband, Ravinder ‘Monu’ Kaliramna, has been working along the same lines. The plan was always to use the CWG as part of the build-up, with the Asian Games in mind.Seema's own assessment after the 57.44m throw was similarly measured.“It is not that bad. According to the Asian Games, it is good.”That calmness took time to build. Seema was preparing for the World University Games after her marriage in 2019 and says she was throwing 54-55m in training. A knee injury and then COVID kept her away from competition. She continued training around the same distance but could not get the competitions she needed.Then came pregnancy and childbirth.Seema gave birth to her son Rudra in 2022. He is now four years old. She returned to competitive competition 11 months after his birth, but the period around pregnancy and childbirth had left her dealing with severe physical problems.After giving birth, Seema's physical problems became severe. She has described how her shoulder and hip had become frozen during pregnancy and how the condition worsened after delivery. Doctors told her she had severe arthritis.“At that time, I was not able to walk up to 10 meters, and I was not able to pick up my child.”At one point, she wondered whether continuing to live like that was possible.“In such a condition, a person thinks that instead of living like this, it is better not to live.”She had not simply stopped throwing, but she had to work out whether her body could return to the sport at all. Ravinder's answer was to start again, but according to her body.“My husband said that we will start the game again. We will take her according to her body, as and when the muscle develops, the arthritis will reduce.”It did.Seema returned to competition in 2024. Her competition best before motherhood had been 48.08m. She went to 57.19m in 2024, won the 2025 National Games, and then moved beyond 59m this season.Seema's return to the throwing circle was not something she worked through on her own.Ravinder was there as her coach, but he was also the person beside her through pregnancy, the arthritis that followed and the long process of getting her body ready to compete again. The two have also been working towards the same Olympic goal. For Seema, that makes it difficult to separate the two roles.“When you have a goal, when you are living a dream… we are living the same dream, so there is not much difference between us.”Their sporting set-up has also been supported by the Inspire Institute of Sport, which has provided Seema with physiotherapy, massage, travel, accommodation and other support.“We don't even have a government job, we don't even have a private job, so from physio, to massage, to travelling, accommodation, everything is done by IIS. I have got full support from IIS,” Seema said.However, there was some movement on that front recently. At a Haryana government programme in Panchkula on August 26, Seema said she was approached about a junior coach's position.For now, though, the discus remains the priority. So does Rudra, even when he is not at the stadium.Before the CWG, Seema had spoken about how difficult it was to leave her son behind. In Glasgow, she won bronze and then spoke about missing him. Before she left for the CWG, Seema knew what Rudra was hoping she would bring back - a medal; and she did.He will not be travelling with her to the Asian Games either.A medal will make the trip back home again, just as it did after the CWG. Seema hopes that, one day, Rudra will be the one travelling to competitions - and that she and Monu will be the ones going with him.“He cannot go with me now, but we will make him [raise him in a way] so that in the future he goes out and we go with him.”For now, Rudra will again watch from home, and Seema will go back into the circle, with a CWG bronze behind her, a 59.73m personal best beside her name and an Asian Games medal somewhere ahead.And she is already thinking beyond that. After winning at Glasgow, her first reaction was not about the distance or the podium. Instead, it was: “We did it.”Now she wants the Asian Games to be another step. “So, we will climb one more step towards the Olympics after winning a medal at the Asian Games.”
Article Summary: Seema Kaliramna won Commonwealth Games bronze in discus in Glasgow. The 27-year- old returned to competition in Bhubaneswar on August 22. She threw 59.73m in her first competition since the Commonwealth Games. The Asian Games begin in Japan on September 19.

Article Title: ‘KL is klutch’: Delhi Capitals put KL Rahul trade rumours to bed with blunt message
Article Text:
Delhi Capitals' KL Rahul (ANI Photo)

KL Rahul post

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Delhi Capitals have put an end to speculation surrounding KL Rahul’s future, making it clear that the wicketkeeper-batter remains an important part of their plans and is not heading to any other franchise.Rumours about a potential trade involving Rahul had gathered momentum on social media over the past two weeks, Neither the franchise nor Rahul had officially addressed the speculation until Delhi Capitals co-owner Parth Jindal broke his silence.Jindal made it clear that Delhi have no intention of parting ways with Rahul, highlighting both his performances and his selfless approach to the team.“KL IS KLUTCH FOR @DelhiCapitals - one of the nicest guys I know and one who puts the team before himself always. We have unfinished business and will work hard together to make Delhi proud @IPL,” Jindal wrote on X (formerly Twitter).Rahul responded to Jindal’s post, seemingly putting any doubts over his future to rest.“Thank you, can't wait for the coming season,” the Indian batter wrote.The speculation surrounding Rahul gained traction after Delhi added Rishabh Pant to their squad earlier this year, having traded Kuldeep Yadav to Lucknow Super Giants (LSG).The arrival of Pant means Delhi now have two established wicketkeeping options, while both players have experience of leading teams. Axar Patel remains another leadership option, although his position could come under scrutiny following Delhi's disappointing results in the 2025 and 2026 editions.Despite that combination, Jindal's comments suggest Delhi see Rahul as central to their plans rather than someone they are looking to move on.Rahul has also provided the franchise with considerable consistency since joining them. In his first two seasons with Delhi, he crossed the 1,000-run mark, establishing himself as one of their most reliable batters at the top of the order.With Pant expected to take over the wicketkeeping responsibilities, Rahul could now have greater freedom to focus solely on his batting. That could also open the possibility of the two India stars forming an opening partnership for Delhi.The speculation intensified despite the absence of any official indication that a trade was being discussed. Delhi eventually responded to the noise by posting a video with the caption, “Keep the noise coming.”Jindal's latest post, however, has offered a much more direct response.Rahul is coming off a productive 2026 campaign in which he scored 593 runs for Delhi, finishing fourth in the tournament's run-scoring charts. His standout performance came against Shreyas Iyer's Punjab Kings at the Arun Jaitley Stadium, where he smashed an unbeaten 152, the highest individual score by an Indian in the league.Rahul's innings contained nine sixes and came at a strike rate of 226.9, although Delhi's huge total was ultimately chased down by Punjab Kings.For now, though, the message from Delhi is clear: Rahul remains part of their plans, with Jindal insisting that the franchise still has “unfinished business” with the senior batter.
Article Summary: Delhi Capitals co-owner Parth Jindal breaks his silence on KL Rahul. Jindal says Delhi have 'unfinished business' with Rahul. Delhi added Rishabh Pant to their squad earlier this year, having traded Kuldeep Yadav to Lucknow Super Giants.

Article Title: ‘Maybe I’m just getting older’: Naomi Osaka’s surprising reaction after US Open exit
Article Text:
Naomi Osaka (AP Photo)

‘I'm happy I'm taking losses differently’

Osaka's fashion showcase lights up New York

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

‘If I win another Grand Slam, it's not going to change my life’

Naomi Osaka's US Open campaign came to an end in the fourth round, but the former world No. 1 walked away from Flushing Meadows with a sense of perspective rather than disappointment.The two-time US Open champion was beaten by Elena Rybakina in a one-sided contest on Monday, ending a run that had also seen Osaka once again capture attention away from the court with a series of eye-catching fashion statements.Yet when she addressed the media after the defeat, Osaka's focus was less on the loss and more on the bigger picture.Asked whether she was disappointed that her exit meant fans would not get to see some of the other fashion looks she may have planned for later rounds, Osaka admitted there was always something in the works."I think there's always something [laughs]. That's a way that I can have fun and sort of just excite myself also. But I'm honestly not disappointed now. It's a very strange feeling. And last year I wasn't that disappointed either. Amanda just played really insane. Maybe I'm just getting older, but I don't feel sad."The four-time Grand Slam champion was then asked whether she was surprised by her reaction to the defeat, given that losses had often affected her more deeply earlier in her career.Osaka said she has learned to process setbacks differently and now looks for lessons rather than dwelling on disappointment."I think I'm happy I'm taking losses differently. I'm trying to learn from them a lot more. Today if I was to say I'm sad, I was sad that I couldn't push off on my foot. I'm sad I couldn't do what I set out to do."The 28-year-old revealed she had been troubled by pain in her leg during the match against Rybakina, which affected her movement on court.Still, she stressed that tennis results no longer define her outlook on life."But for me if I think about my life, my daughter is healthy. Everyone in my family is great. I had an opportunity to play this Slam. I got as far as I could. It's only up from here I guess."Although her tournament ended in the fourth round, Osaka remained one of the standout personalities of the event thanks to a string of fashion-forward appearances inspired by basketball culture.With sponsor Nike celebrating the New York Knicks' championship triumph, Osaka unveiled a different look throughout the tournament, working alongside celebrity stylist Law Roach.For her final appearance, she arrived on court wearing a fur-trimmed multicoloured cloak designed by Brooklyn-based label KidSuper."I felt really swaggy when I put it on," Osaka said after the match. "I feel feel like it embodied New York a lot."The outfit also featured a headband inspired by the NBA logo, replacing the traditional basketball player silhouette with a tennis player holding a racket.Earlier in the tournament, Osaka paid tribute to NBA legend Allen Iverson with a dramatic first-round ensemble designed by Who Decides War, featuring a long white tulle skirt, a hooded robe and cornrows beneath a headband reminiscent of Iverson's iconic style.Her second-round look came from Thom Browne and included a flowing white jacket embroidered with crossed tennis rackets, while the mesh fabric of her skirt was designed to resemble a basketball net.For the third round, she wore an oversized Monse outfit that blended a suit jacket and hoodie with flowing fleece trousers, combining businesswear and sportswear aesthetics.Osaka's comments after the loss reflected a broader shift in how she now views her career and achievements.While still motivated to compete at the highest level, the former world No. 1 suggested that winning another major title would not fundamentally alter her life or sense of fulfilment.Reflecting on everything she has already achieved in the sport, Osaka indicated she no longer measures happiness solely through victories and trophies."Maybe I'm just getting older, but I don't feel sad," Osaka said. "I think, also, if I reflect on my career and the things that I've been able to do, there's nothing that I regret or there's nothing that I'm sad about ... If I win another Grand Slam, it's not going to change my life."For Osaka, the US Open may have ended earlier than she hoped, but her reaction to defeat suggested a player increasingly at peace with both her career and her life beyond tennis.
Article Summary: Naomi Osaka's US Open campaign came to an end in the fourth round. The former world No. 1 was beaten by Elena Rybakina in a one-sided contest. The 28-year-old revealed she had been troubled by pain in her leg during the match. Osaka said she has learned to process setbacks differently.

Article Title: Indian Olympic Association set for governance reset ahead of December polls
Article Text:
P T Usha

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) will convene a Special General Body Meeting (SGBM) on Tuesday to adopt its amended constitution in line with the national sports governance act, 2025, in what is set to be a significant constitutional exercise for the apex Olympic body ahead of its elections, which sees the first four-year term of P T Usha-led executive committee (EC) coming to an end later this year.The SGBM will formally adopt the constitution, paving the way for its eventual ratification by the IOA General Body in the coming months. The exercise assumes significance with the IOA's current executive term ending in Dec 2026 and elections having to be conducted under the new governance framework.All affiliated national sports federations (NSFs) and State Olympic Associations (SOAs) are expected to attend the meeting, scheduled ahead of the official send-off ceremony for the Indian contingent for the Asian Games on the same day. The meeting will bring together the IOA's members to discuss and adopt the constitutional provisions required under the new law.The amendments are necessary before the IOA can proceed with its election process. Football, athletics and cycling are among the early NSFs to have already amended their constitutions in line with the Act, sources said.The SGBM will also assume importance in the process of appointing the Returning Officer (RO) for the IOA elections.The constitutional changes need to be adopted and subsequently ratified so that the election machinery can be put in place under the new statutory framework, with the polls required to be held on or before December 10.Selected provisions of the Act came into force on Jan 1, 2026. While several federations have begun aligning their constitutions, some are finding the exercise difficult. A key challenge is the requirement for executive committees to have no more than 15 members, with some federations struggling to restructure their existing bodies accordingly.Others are facing difficulties in identifying Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit (SOMs), while provisions relating to age limits, tenure and cooling-off periods have also emerged as issues.The National Sports Board (NSB), envisaged under the Act, will have the power to grant recognition to or derecognise NSFs. The Indian cricket board (BCCI), too, will ultimately have to fall within the Act’s regulatory ambit. Once the NSB becomes operational and the new framework takes full shape, the BCCI will have to apply for fresh recognition as a national sports body and conduct its elections according to the Act.
Article Summary: The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) will convene a Special General Body Meeting (SGBM) on Tuesday to adopt its amended constitution in line with the national sports governance act, 2025. The SGBM will formally adopt the constitution, paving the way for its eventual ratification by the IOA General Body in the coming months. All affiliated national sports federations (NSFs) and State Olympic Associations (SOAs) are expected to attend the meeting.

Article Title: PV Sindhu’s physio gets Asian Games green light despite BAI's snub
Article Text:
PV Sindhu competes against China's Wang Zhi Yi, unseen, in a women's singles badminton match during the BWF World Championships, at IGI Stadium, in New Delhi. (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Delhi: PV Sindhu will have almost her entire support staff spearheading her medal campaign at the Asian Games, with the sports ministry clearing the names of her personal physiotherapist Heera Mundluru and strength and conditioning coach Shreyasi Sanjay.Coaching staffer Muhammad Irwansyah, who has been appointed as India’s women’s singles coach but will largely focus on Sindhu’s game and technique, has also received official sanction.Interestingly, Mundluru’s name was not recommended by the Badminton Association of India (BAI). That, however, did little to stop the sanctioning authorities, who cleared her inclusion, ensuring Sindhu has the support system she needs.Long jumper Shahnavaz Khan, too, has been sanctioned his personal coach Bhupinder Singh, while Ancy Sojan will have Anoop Joseph by her side.In table tennis, former India player Soumyadeep Roy has been cleared as coach for Payas Jain, Cinderella Das and Sutirtha Mukherjee, giving several medal hopefuls familiar support at the Aichi-Nagoya Games.
Article Summary: PV Sindhu will have almost her entire support staff spearheading her medal campaign at the Asian Games. The sports ministry has cleared the names of her personal physiotherapist Heera Mundluru and strength and conditioning coach Shreyasi Sanjay. Muhammad Irwansyah, who has been appointed as India’s women's singles coach, has also received official sanction. Long jumper Shahnavaz Khan has been sanctioned his personal coach Bhupinder Singh.

Article Title: In attack mode: Satwik-Chirag train their eyes on Asian Games
Article Text:
Satwiksairaj Rankireddy, left, and Chirag Shetty clinch China Masters Super 750 title after defeating China's He Ji Ting and Ren Xiang Yu in a three-game thriller, in Shenzhen, China. (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A day after becoming the first Indian pair to win the China Masters title, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty have now trained their sights on the Asian Games, where they defend the men's doubles gold they won in 2023.The duo remain the only Indian shuttlers to have won gold at the Asian Games, but Chirag insists there is no added pressure to repeat that feat. "We want to go out there and do what we normally do on court. If we're able to do that, I think we'll go deep into the tournament, and that's the only thing we want," said Chirag during a virtual interaction arranged by the Badminton Association of India (BAI) on Monday."We don't want to think too much about the results. When we keep the results aside and take one match at a time, that's when we play our best."The Indians head into the Continental Games in ominous form, riding on their stirring victory in Shenzhen.Chirag believes the pair's biggest challenges will come from two contrasting styles. He rated Korea's Kim Won Ho and Seo Seung Jae as the best defensive combination on the circuit, while world champions Liang Wei Keng and Wang Chang of China remain the most potent attacking pair, albeit a notch below the Indians."Apart from us, I think Liang and Wang are the best attacking players. When it comes to defence, it's Kim Won Ho and Seo Seung Jae," Chirag said.He also acknowledged that his own defensive game still has room for improvement."I've added a few new aspects to my defence, but there's still a lot to be done," he said.Kim and Seo, who won 11 titles last year, began 2026 in equally dominant fashion, claiming three successive titles before Satwik and Chirag ended their streak with a semifinal victory at the Singapore Open on May 31.Since then, the Korean world No. 1 pair has endured a lean spell, failing to win a title in their next six tournaments. Their slump also included a first round exit at the China Masters, where the Indians went on to lift the trophy.For Satwik and Chirag, however, the blueprint remains unchanged. Even if their trademark attacking game is neutralised, Satwik says there is no alternative approach. "It's always Plan A - there's no Plan B for us.But it depends on the opponents. It's never easy. They don't want to lift the shuttle to us either," he said. "Whether it's the Malaysians, Indonesians or even the Chinese, everyone wants to play fast and get into the attack rather than give us a target. "Satwik also underlined the importance of Chirag's presence at the front of the court, saying his partner's ability to create openings has made his finishing role considerably easier. "Chirag makes my job so much easier - he creates so many chances for me to finish," he said.
Article Summary: Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty are the only Indian shuttlers to have won gold at the Asian Games. The pair won the China Masters Super 750 title on Sunday, becoming the first Indian pair to do so. They will now defend the men's doubles gold they won in 2023. The duo say their biggest challenges will come from two contrasting styles.

Article Title: ‘Inexplicable': Karun Nair takes subtle dig at South Zone after being overlooked for Duleep Trophy final
Article Text:
Karun Nair

Karun Nair's Post

South Zone struggle as Ishan Kishan produces 270

Kishan falls 30 short of triple century

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Karnataka batter Karun Nair has taken a subtle but pointed swipe at South Zone after being overlooked for the playing XI in the ongoing Duleep Trophy final against East Zone at the MA Chidambaram Stadium.Nair, who was part of the South Zone squad, was left out of the XI for both the semi-final and the final. After a post on X (formerly Twitter) described his omission as ‘inexplicable’, Nair reposted it with his own response.‘Inexplicable would be an understatement,’ he wrote, accompanied by a laughing emoji.The decision has gained further attention after South Zone endured a difficult first two days of the final, with East Zone piling up 708 runs before being bowled out.Nair did not remain with the South Zone squad after learning that he would not feature in the final. Instead, he returned home to join the Karnataka State Cricket Association's pre-season red-ball camp.The batter then made an immediate impact, scoring a century for KSCA Secretary XI against Chhattisgarh.South Zone have not provided an explanation for Nair's omission from the playing XI for the final. His absence had already raised eyebrows before the previous match against North Zone, when captain Tilak Varma explained that Nair's exclusion was a tactical call.At the time, Varma said Nair was ‘just unlucky’ after opting for Hyderabad's left-handed batter Kodimela Himateja in the middle order.“Karun is just unlucky. He has scored a lot of runs in domestic seasons," Tilak had said while addressing the media at the CoE.“I have chosen Himateja in place of Karun as they have good left-arm spinners. So we wanted a leftie in the middle order. He has also scored a decent amount of runs in domestic cricket. I was just backing him. As a youngster, he also has a good career. At the same time, it is very unfortunate for Karun."However, Himateja's opportunity did not work out. He was dismissed for a two-ball duck and subsequently dropped for the final.South Zone replaced him with another left-hander, Devdutt Padikkal, rather than bringing Nair back into the XI.The omission of Nair has become an even bigger talking point after South Zone's bowling attack struggled to contain East Zone in the final.East Zone resumed the second innings on 385/4 and continued to dominate from the outset. South Zone took the new ball after one over, hoping Mohammad Siraj and MD Nidheesh could make early inroads, but neither managed to break the partnership between Ishan Kishan and Kumar Kushagra.Kishan immediately attacked Siraj and Nidheesh, while Kushagra provided strong support from the other end. South Zone subsequently turned to Tripurana Vijay and Shreyas Gopal, but the change in bowling did little to halt the scoring.Kushagra eventually completed his sixth first-class century, making 101 from 132 balls with eight fours and five sixes before falling to Vijay shortly before lunch.Kishan then took complete control of the innings.The East Zone captain repeatedly found the boundary and took advantage of a tiring South Zone attack. Even the introduction of part-timers Devdutt Padikkal and Shaikh Rasheed failed to slow him down.Kishan reached his double century from 270 balls and continued attacking, moving beyond 250 before briefly retiring because of fatigue.East Zone eventually crossed 600 and then moved towards the 700-run mark. Mohammed Shami's quickfire 28 helped push the total closer to the landmark before his dismissal brought Kishan back to the crease.The East Zone skipper returned with a triple century in sight, but South Zone finally managed to remove him before he could reach the milestone.Kishan was caught near the long-on boundary for a stunning 270 off 334 balls, an innings containing 30 fours and seven sixes. His score ranks as the eighth-highest individual innings in Duleep Trophy history.East Zone were eventually dismissed for 708, registering a total above 700 at Chepauk for only the third time in first-class cricket history.The mammoth score has put East Zone firmly in control of the final and added another layer to the questions surrounding Nair's omission.For Nair, meanwhile, his brief response on social media has made his feelings about being left out fairly clear, particularly after South Zone's bowling attack was unable to contain Kishan and Kushagra in the final.
Article Summary: Karnataka batter Karun Nair takes a swipe at South Zone after being overlooked for the playing XI in the ongoing Duleep Trophy final. Nair was left out of the XI for both the semi-final and the final. The decision has gained further attention after South Zone endured a difficult first two days of the final with East Zone piling up 708 runs.

Article Title: Stage set for Rajasthan Cricket Association elections on September 29 as administrator Sawant issues notice
Article Text:
Sawai Mansingh Stadium in Jaipur, Rajasthan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

JAIPUR: The wheels are officially in motion for the Rajasthan Cricket Association (RCA) elections, following a formal notification issued on Monday by its state-appointed administrator Bhaskar A Sawant. The notice calls for the Annual General Meeting (AGM) and elections to the executive committee for the 2026–2029 term, scheduled to take place on Sept 29 at 11:00am at the RCA Academy here.Former state election commissioner AK Pandey (IAS retd), has been appointed as the independent electoral officer to oversee the polling process, assisted by Pushpendra Singh Hada, former district judge, as assistant electoral officer.A critical element of the upcoming election centers on the composition of the electoral college. The voter list has been expanded to include three newly formed district units - Didwana-Kuchaman, Balotra, and Khairthal-Tijara - alongside designated representatives from existing affiliated District Cricket Associations (DCAs) across the state. The eligible voting pool also features registered former international players, with ex-international cricketers Gagan Khoda and Pankaj Singh explicitly named on the electoral roll.Conversely, district units currently operating without elected executives are represented through convenors of ad hoc committees, such as Rajesh Kumar Tambi for DCA Jaipur and Rajesh Bishnoi for DCA Nagaur. Furthermore, per High Court orders dated June 16, 2026, representatives from the Sawai Madhopur DCA remain barred from participating or voting in the AGM pending further judicial proceedings.Copies of the official election notice have been formally dispatched to key stakeholders, including the secretary and CEO of Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI), the Rajasthan State Sports Council, and the registrar of co-operative societies, Jaipur.The nomination process for candidates seeking to contest the RCA elections will take place from Sept 23-26. After nominations are filed, the nomination papers will be scrutinized on Sept 27, and eligible candidates will be published. Candidates will be allowed to withdraw their nominations until Sept 28, leading up to the final voting and counting of votes scheduled for Sept 29, when the results will be declared on the same day.The election will decide six key executive positions on the RCA apex council: president, vice-president, secretary, joint-secretary, treasurer and one executive member. Alongside the elections, the general body will confirm the minutes from the Extraordinary General Body Meeting held on June 26, 2026, and consider the formal adoption of the audited statement of accounts for the 2024–25 financial year.
Article Summary: The Rajasthan Cricket Association (RCA) elections will take place on Sept 29. The election will decide six key executive positions on the RCA apex council. The voter list has been expanded to include three newly formed district units. The eligible voting pool also features registered former international players.

Article Title: I wish I had Pirlo's intelligence: Cafu
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

KOLKATA: As the city is preparing to host Carlo Ancelotti's Brazil in a historic international friendly with India next month, Cafu's whirlwind visit here on Monday came with a whiff of nostalgia and longing.The former Sao Paulo, AS Roma and AC Milan defender had led Brazil to their fifth World Cup crown back in 2002 and the Selecao have since struggled to scale the ultimate peak in world football.The 56-year-old didn't reflect on what's ailing Brazilian football right now, but he did open up on a few interesting topics during a rapid-fire round with former Mohun Bagan captain and fellow Brazilian Jose Ramirez Barreto acting as the interviewer."I wish I had Pirlo's football intelligence," Cafu said in reply to Barreto's query about whose quality he would like to 'steal' given a chance.Cafu and Pirlo had played together at AC Milan from 2003 to 2008 when Ancelotti had been in charge of the Italian team. It is still hailed as the golden period for the Italian giants who went on to win two Uefa Champions League titles and one Fifa Club World Cup crown among others during the time."And who's that one player you wish you could have played with but never got a chance?" Barreto asked during the programme hosted by the Bengal National Chamber of Commerce and Industry."It has to be Maradona," pat came the reply from the Brazilian who is the only player to have played in three World Cup title-deciders, "because I've played with Pele (in an exhibition match)."According to him, Ronaldo was more frightening than Romario as "an opponent."Cafu featured in an exhibition match by women footballers during the inauguration of AADAC Education Foundation before calling on chief minister Suvendu Adhikari at Nabanna. Before leaving, he gave Indian football a word of advice. "Believe in yourself. That's all. "
Article Summary: Cafu is in India ahead of Brazil's friendly with India next month. The former Sao Paulo, AS Roma and AC Milan defender had led Brazil to their fifth World Cup crown back in 2002. The 56-year-old didn't reflect on what's ailing Brazilian football right now, but did open up on a few interesting topics.

Article Title: Young East Bengal live up to ‘senior’ Bagan’s challenge in CFL derby
Article Text:
Mohun Bagan With First-Team Players Are Held 1-1 In CFL Derby

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

KOLKATA: Eventually, there were no winners in the CFL Premier Division derby at Barasat on Monday.A heavily reinforced Mohun Bagan failed to make Manvir Singh's first-half strike count as East Bengal FC came back with renewed vigour and vision after the break and duly scooped up the equaliser through Mohamed Bilal's powerful header, ensuring that it remained even-steven. Yet, the way East Bengal FC players were celebrating after the match manifested the underlying current of this latest clash between the two traditional rivals.With both the teams having already qualified for the championship round, Monday's face-off looked more to be a game of academic interest than anything else. Yet Mohun Bagan decided to inject life into it by pitchforking a host of senior-team players into the field and trying to make the most of it. If there was a need to end their 12-year-long winless run against the rivals in the local league, Mohun Bagan's competitive drive was further accentuated by the fact that the match was happening just a fortnight after they suffered a 1-4 capitulation to East Bengal in the Durand Cup final.So, the way senior team coach Panagiotis Dilmperis helped his assistant Bastab Roy prepare for the match and the likes of Subhashis Bose, Apuia, Sahal Abdul Samad, Rahul Bheke and Manvir were given the start on Monday, Mohun Bagan's search for a revenge was all too evident at the outset.East Bengal, however, decided to keep faith in their proven performers from the reserve side which not only entered the contest with an unbeaten run in this league but was determined to live up to the challenge.The game started off on predictable lines - Bagan dominating possession and East Bengal fighting tooth and nail to keep them at bay.Manvir eventually broke the deadlock in the 38th minute. Racing into the box and facing a challenge from Ankan Bhattacharjee, the Bagan attacker drove home, although East Bengal goalkeeper Gourab Shaw should have dealt with it.East Bengal returned after the break with more attacking ambitions and the Bagan backline - manned by three senior pros - captain Subhashis, Bheke and Mehtab Singh - had a tough time in containing them. Mehtab denied Akash Hemram with a timely intervention while Bijay Murmu hit the side-netting from close. Bilal eventually made it 1-1 in the 65th minute. Ten minutes after substituting Manotosh Maji, Bilal met Murmu's corner with a sumptuous header, giving Bagan goalkeeper Deeprobhat Ghosh no chance to react.Bagan still came calling but Sayan Banerjee was denied by Shaw's brilliant finger-tipping save. At the other end, East Bengal's Uttam Hansda saw his header ricochet off the crosspiece.Bagan heaved a sigh of relief as a spirited and young East Bengal showed them that it was never meant to be a child's play.The draw helped East Bengal pip Bhawanipore SC to the top of Group A with a better goal difference while Bagan would enter the Super 6 with 23 points, four points behind the duo.
Article Summary: Mohun Bagan failed to make Manvir Singh's first-half strike count as East Bengal FC came back with renewed vigour and vision after the break. Mohamed Bilal's powerful header ensured that it remained even-steven. The draw helped East Bengal pip Bhawanipore SC to the top of Group A with a better goal difference.

Article Title: ‘Learn from Ishan Kishan’: Ex-India cricketer’s message to Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
Article Text:
Ishan Kishan - Vaibhav Sooryavanshi

Ishan Kishan takes East Zone past 700

Kishan falls 30 short of triple century

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi may have been among the early contributors for East Zone in the Duleep Trophy final, but it was captain Ishan Kishan who eventually stole the show with a breathtaking double century against South Zone at the MA Chidambaram Stadium.Sooryavanshi opened the innings for East Zone and made a brisk 44 off 37 deliveries. During the match, former India cricketer and commentator Vivek Razdan used Kishan's remarkable innings to offer some advice to the teenage batter."Sooryavanshi sahab, now you have to learn from players like Ishan Kishan. Once you are set, you have to learn how to play a long innings," Razdan said on commentary.The message came as Kishan continued to pile on the runs and turn the final into a one-sided contest.Resuming on 385/4, East Zone's batters showed little sign of slowing down. South Zone turned to the new ball in search of wickets, but Mohammad Siraj and MD Nidheesh struggled to make an impact.Kishan immediately put pressure on the bowlers, collecting consecutive boundaries against Siraj before taking on Nidheesh. Kumar Kushagra also joined the assault as South Zone rotated between pace and spin.Kushagra eventually completed his sixth first-class century, scoring 101 from 132 balls with eight fours and five sixes.His dismissal shortly before lunch finally gave South Zone a breakthrough.Kishan, meanwhile, remained in complete control.The East Zone captain repeatedly found gaps in the field and punished anything loose. Even when South Zone introduced part-timers Devdutt Padikkal and Shaikh Rasheed, the flow of runs did not stop.Kishan brought up his double century from 270 balls and continued attacking thereafter. He raced beyond 250 before fatigue briefly forced him to retire from the field.East Zone continued marching towards a massive total, eventually crossing 600 and then 700. When Mohammed Shami was dismissed for a quick 28, Kishan returned to the crease with the possibility of reaching an extraordinary triple century.Kishan's pursuit of 300 ultimately came to an end when he was caught near the long-on boundary. The left-hander departed for a monumental 270 from 334 balls, having smashed 30 fours and seven sixes.His innings was the eighth-highest individual score in Duleep Trophy history and formed the backbone of East Zone's mammoth 708 all out.Razdan had earlier highlighted not just the quality of Kishan's batting but also the physical demands of staying at the crease for such an extended period."Every person who is present here at this time stood up and applauded this innings. Because this is not just technique, this is not just temperament, this is also match fitness. To stay out there for so long in such heat and play an innings like this. What an innings by Ishan Kishan."Kishan's marathon effort, alongside Kushagra's century, ensured East Zone posted more than 700 for only the third time in first-class cricket history at Chepauk.For Sooryavanshi, who had already made an impact with his 44, Razdan's message was clear: scoring quickly is only part of the equation. The next step is learning how to convert a start into a substantial innings, much like Kishan did in the Duleep Trophy final.
Article Summary: Ishan Kishan scores 270 from 334 balls in East Zone's 708 all out. Former India cricketer Vivek Razdan gives advice to young batsman. Kumar Kushagra scores 101 from 132 balls for South Zone.

Article Title: Will Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli play the 2027 ODI World Cup? Ashish Nehra says 'Why not?'
Article Text:
Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli (BCCI Photo)

Nehra has no regrets over 2003 World Cup final

‘I always look forward’

‘Coaching India would be a great honour’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Will Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma play in the 2027 ODI World Cup? It is one of the biggest questions for Indian cricket fans.The next 50-over World Cup will be held in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia in 2027. Rohit will be 40 and Kohli 39 when the tournament begins.Former India pacer Ashish Nehra, however, does not want to make any prediction about the two veterans' future.Nehra said performances can change the situation quickly and it is too early to say whether Rohit and Kohli will still be part of India's ODI plans."We have seen, not in Indian cricket but in any sport, that even 2-3 weeks before, things change. If they are doing well, if they are performing, why not? It's not going to be easy for any coach or any captain when it comes to these players."We all know, we don't need to discuss what they have done in the past. For 13 months, a long time, it is very difficult to say right now that Rohit or Virat will be there. I mean, for those guys, age is no number. I'm saying no to any certainty."Yes, we talk about Shubman Gill, we talk Bumrah, but the same Gill is not in T20 sport. The way he is playing is fast-speed sport in more formats. It is difficult to say. It is too early for me."Nehra also looked back at India's 125-run defeat to Australia in the 2003 World Cup final at the Wanderers.The former India pacer was part of that Indian team but said he does not spend time regretting the defeat."Not really. What's gone is gone. It's always a good learning. It was not the only final I played, and we lost. I played some other finals also, and we lost. Every time you don't win, yes, as a player, you are always gutted when you look back, but it's not only me."There are so many players, I am sure, in international cricket, who have lost more finals than the final we were discussing."Nehra compared India's 2003 World Cup campaign with the team's run in the 2023 ODI World Cup, where India lost to Australia in the final in Ahmedabad.He felt both teams had enjoyed strong campaigns before falling short in the final."The whole tournament, we were playing well, in the 2023 50-over World Cup in India, our team was no different, and exactly the final we lost in Ahmedabad."In fact, we were more dominating than we were in 2003, but that's part and parcel of the game. I never look back, and I'm not somebody who regrets too much. I always look forward."Nehra was also asked whether he would like to become India's head coach someday.The former India pacer said he does not plan his career in advance, but admitted that coaching India would be a huge honour."First thing first, I will not use the word ambition. I never plan. Yes, it will be a great honour and a privilege, but I never plan things like that. We'll see in the future. No, no ambition. I'm very happy where I am."When it comes to GT, lots of people say like you have done well in coaching. It's not me; it's about the team. Yes, when your captain, when your coach is always associated, that's the way it goes, especially in India, but I'm dead against it. When it comes to team sport, it should not be like Shubman Gill won, or Nehra won, but it should be GT won," he said.
Article Summary: The next 50-over World Cup will be held in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia in 2027. Rohit will be 40 and Kohli 39 when the tournament begins. Ashish Nehra does not want to make any prediction about the two veterans' future.

Article Title: ‘Pakistan cricket has gone back 10 years’: Saeed Ajmal launches scathing PCB attack
Article Text:
Chairman of Pakistan Cricket Board Mohsin Naqvi, centre, chats with Pakistan's Babar Azam, left, as head coach Mike Hesson watches (AP Photo)

Ajmal points finger at Aaqib Javed , Mike Hesson

Mohsin Naqvi defends PCB's decision to make changes

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former Pakistan spinner Saeed Ajmal has launched another scathing attack on the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB), accusing the governing body of playing a major role in the national team's recent struggles.Ajmal, who claimed 362 wickets across international cricket for Pakistan before his career was brought to an early end by an issue with his bowling action, has repeatedly expressed his frustration with the PCB. The former spinner has maintained that the board failed to support him during a difficult phase of his career.His latest criticism comes after Pakistan suffered another heavy defeat against England in the Lord's Test. Following the loss, the PCB made a series of sweeping changes, sacking head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul while also sending seven players back home.Among those sent back was Imam-ul-Haq, who did not bat in either innings and was subsequently accused of faking his calf injury.PCB chairman Mohsin Naqvi later attempted to defend the players and urged critics to stop demotivating the team. Ajmal, however, questioned the sincerity of that message and instead accused the board itself of undermining Pakistan's cricketers."The board itself has demotivated the players more than anyone else. The board is not letting any player stand. There are players who have done well, who have also been dropped. There are players who have been humiliated by the PCB," Ajmal said.The former Pakistan spinner also directed his criticism towards Director High Performance and selector Aaqib Javed and white-ball head coach Mike Hesson.With Hesson also asked to take charge of the Test side for the third match against England, Ajmal claimed the pair have significant control over Pakistan cricket and held them responsible for the team's current situation."Aaqib Javed and Mike Hesson (who has been asked to take over the Test team for the third Test) are a team. These two are controlling everything and are responsible for this whole mess. The whole issue is about egos," Ajmal said on Samaa TV.Ajmal further criticised the PCB's long-term planning, claiming Pakistan's cricket structure had regressed considerably."Our team has gone back 10 years. We have not planned for the future," he added.Pakistan have already surrendered the Test series against England and are now facing the prospect of a clean sweep. The third and final Test is scheduled to begin at Edgbaston on Wednesday, with Hesson set to take charge of the Test side.Naqvi, meanwhile, had earlier attempted to explain the reasoning behind the PCB's decision to make such extensive changes after the Lord's defeat.Speaking to Geo Network, the PCB chairman insisted that the decisions were not motivated by personal issues and said the board had little choice when players were not producing results."Every match of a series is important for us, and we are not left with any option if a player is not performing but to look for his replacement. The purpose behind these changes is not to axe players from contention, but just to replace them. Consider [Salman] Agha, who is a very good player, but he could not click because of some reasons. He was spoken to about it," he said.Naqvi's comments were aimed at stressing that the changes should not be viewed as permanent exclusions or personal vendettas.Ajmal, however, has taken a markedly different view, arguing that the PCB's repeated decisions to remove players and coaches have contributed to instability within the Pakistan team.With Pakistan now one defeat away from an England series whitewash, the pressure on the board, coaching staff and players has intensified further.
Article Summary: Saeed Ajmal has launched another scathing attack on the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) The former spinner has repeatedly expressed his frustration with the board. His latest criticism comes after Pakistan suffered another heavy defeat against England in the Lord's Test. The third and final Test is scheduled to begin at Edgbaston on Wednesday.

Article Title: 'North pole and south pole': Ashish Nehra compares Shubman Gill and Hardik Pandya as captains
Article Text:
Hardik Pandya and Shubman Gill (BCCI/IPL Photo)

'Gill observes more and to the point'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Shubman Gill is still learning the art of captaincy and will improve with experience, Gujarat Titans head coach Ashish Nehra said on Monday.Gill took over as Gujarat Titans captain after Hardik Pandya left the franchise. He led the team to the IPL final in 2026, after Pandya and Nehra had guided GT to the title in their first season in 2022 and another final in 2023.Nehra said Gill and Pandya are very different personalities and leaders, but both have the ability to keep learning."They are very, very different. You are talking about north pole and south pole. Both of them were like me, not somebody who has done much coaching," Nehra said, comparing Pandya and Gill."Both of them were not somebody who has done much captaincy, but you learn on your way forward, and suddenly somebody is pretty much doing captaincy for India in two formats. He is only going to get better."Nehra said Pandya was very open with him and trusted him completely during their successful partnership at Gujarat Titans.Gill, on the other hand, is quieter and more reserved but remains eager to learn."One thing is for sure: he (Pandya) completely trusted me, which was the perfect, perfect thing. He will always be keen to learn. He will always ask if something doesn't go right or doesn't go well.He is somebody you can have lots of conversations with," Nehra said."The other way around, Shubman is a little reserved, a little shy, but that's okay. Everyone is different. There is no right or wrong. He (Gill) is someone who will not talk or have as many conversations as Hardik Pandya, but he is to the point. He is somebody who is very keen to learn and keen to observe. Of course, he is a work in progress. He is only 26-27, and it is not that he has been doing captaincy for so many years. It is only 1-2 seasons, and you learn things and you will get better," he said.
Article Summary: Gill took over as Gujarat Titans captain after Hardik Pandya left the franchise. He led the team to the IPL final in 2026, after Pandya and Nehra had guided GT to the title in their first season in 2022. Nehra said Gill and Pandya are very different personalities and leaders.

Article Title: 'Not overthinking, not keeping expectations': Ishan Kishan reveals mindset behind epic 270 in Duleep Trophy final
Article Text:
Ishan Kishan (Image credit: BCCI Domestic)

From India regular to domestic cricket

‘My job as a batsman is just to go there’

Preparing for red-ball cricket

Building partnerships was the key

Kishan reflects on his domestic stint

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Ishan Kishan believes having a clear mind has helped him rediscover his best form. After hitting a stunning 270 in the Duleep Trophy final, East Zone captain Kishan said he has learned to avoid overthinking and putting unnecessary pressure on himself.For Kishan, the focus is now simple - score runs and help his team win matches. His marathon knock against South Zone was a clear sign of the change in his mindset after a difficult phase in his career."I didn't actively try to change myself. It just happened naturally. When I was out of the (India) squad, I realised that we ultimately only have one job to do: simply to score runs. That is the only thing that helps you in your career," Kishan said in the post-day press meet."Any other thoughts will only manipulate your mindset, push you into overthinking, and pile on unnecessary pressure. I realised that those extraneous thoughts aren't necessary. Our job is to step in and win matches for the team. That's all you should care about. You evolve with time, and I feel it is much easier to play this way when you keep your mind clear," he added.Kishan was an all-format India player in 2023, but a series of events saw him lose his place in the team and eventually his BCCI central contract. He then returned to domestic cricket and worked hard to rebuild his career.Kishan scored centuries in the 2025-26 Ranji Trophy and played an important role in Jharkhand's Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy triumph. He scored 517 runs in the tournament, including two hundreds. His strong performances soon earned him a BCCI contract and a return to India's white-ball teams.Kishan said he now tries not to think too much about the result or his position in the team."The best thing I'm doing nowadays is not thinking about anything. My job as a batsman is just to go there, watch the ball, and react to it and not keep any expectations from myself. At times, you will, obviously, lose patience. But that is the time when you have to talk to yourself; you have to control that, calm your thoughts about whether you are taking the right decision or not, and after that, you execute your plans,” he said.Kishan also explained how he prepared for the Duleep Trophy after spending time playing white-ball cricket.“I was here at the BCCI CoE before coming here. We were practicing there, specifically with the red ball. When you play T20s regularly, you start playing a lot of shots — which is what happened in my first innings against the North East Zone (in Duleep Trophy). In the middle, I went to play a cut and then got double-minded about whether to hit it or not and got out.”Ahead of the final, Kishan changed his focus and spent more time building partnerships instead of looking for quick runs.“When you're playing a final and you are already a multi-format player, who has played for India for quite some time, the team members expect you to score runs. So, it's very important for me to be in the middle and get as many runs for your team.“The plan remained simple: keep adding 50-run partnerships as much as possible. A lot of things factor in picking up when their bowlers are tiring, when they are opening up the field—so you keep batting around these things without worrying about the result,” he explained.Kishan said returning to domestic cricket was not something he considered a punishment.Instead, he enjoyed the experience and used the time to reflect on his game and understand where he needed to improve."I genuinely enjoyed it because I went back, had to grind and work hard for about two years (when he was out of the team). But sometimes, what happens is, when we play regularly for the Indian team, you just keep playing in a flow.You might be a very good player which is why you're playing for India, but your growth stagnates at a certain point. So when you take one step back and go back to domestic cricket, you start from zero again."You start thinking, 'I need to get even better,' because today, there are so many players scoring runs. So, to get back into the team, your only option is to perform much better than them.“Nothing against anyone, but I'm saying you'll only benefit if you do better. So, you have to start again. You get time to reflect on what you missed earlier, why you couldn't convert your starts into big scores. The batting doesn't change that much; it's just the mindset that changes over time," he detailed.
Article Summary: Ishan Kishan scored 270 in the Duleep Trophy final for East Zone. The batsman believes having a clear mind has helped him rediscover his best form. He said he tries not to think too much about the result or his position in the team.

Article Title: Rohit Sharma-Virat Kohli threat looms over New Zealand: Mitchell Santner says 'not this time'
Article Text:
Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli (BCCI Photo)

New Zealand want to beat India at home

India tour of New Zealand: Full schedule

Series

‘Very well-rounded’ India squad

‘Fight fire with fire’

Why only two Tests?

New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner is expecting a tough challenge when India’s ODI specialists Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma return to New Zealand later this year. Kohli and Rohit now play only ODI cricket and will be back in action when India tour New Zealand for five ODIs, five T20Is and two Tests in October-November.Santner knows the experienced Indian batters have enjoyed playing in New Zealand in the past. He hopes that will not be the case this time."It is going to be a challenge. They are still very good players as we have seen for a long time; masters of the ODI game. They have taken a liking to some New Zealand pitches in the past. Hopefully, not this time around," Santner told PTI."It is going to be a great series, no doubt. It is all a lead-up for the World Cup next year in ODIs. Everyone is trying to figure out their best team; what that might look like for October next year with limited games."Santner said New Zealand's first target will be to win the ODI series against India at home.The Blackcaps will play five ODIs against India, followed by three ODIs against Sri Lanka at home. They will then travel to England for World Cup preparations in September 2027."We've got five (matches) against India, three against Sri Lanka at home and then it is World Cup prep in England (in September 2027), right before the World Cup," he said."(But) first things first, you want to win a series against India at home, which would be an awesome thing. Then it is (about) trying to find what the make-up might look like come October next year," Santner added.5 T20Is5 ODIs2 TestsIndia and New Zealand last met in a Test series in India, with the Kiwis recording a historic 3-0 win. The result ended India's unbeaten home Test run, which had lasted more than 12 years and 18 series.With India's Test team now going through a change, Santner believes the two-Test series in New Zealand could be difficult for some of the new players."I think what we spoke about before is trying to adapt quickly," said Santner, who took 7/53 and 6/104 in the second Test at Pune to seal the series win, recalling the tour."For a new-look India side, it is probably going to be the first time some players have been playing red-ball (cricket) in New Zealand, where the pitches will be a little bit foreign. They will probably do a bit more than they might do back home."Santner, however, feels India's current Test team is strong and has a good balance.He described the squad as "well-rounded" and said it has been "shaping up nicely"."If you look at their squad, it is a very well-rounded squad. You throw (Jasprit) Bumrah back into the bowling attack, you have got (Mohammed) Siraj, (Prasidh) Krishna with the bounce. You have got (Ravindra) Jadeja and (Manav) Suthar to bowl spin. You have got probably a fourth seamer in there as well.""It is shaping up nicely. I think it is going to be a great series. Traditionally, it can do a little bit in New Zealand at that time of the year," Santner said.Santner also spoke about how teams may need to approach Test cricket in New Zealand. He said batters may have to play their shots at times, while also being ready to defend and see off the new ball.He continued, "It could be trying to fight fire with fire, playing your shots. There might be times we need to sit back and let the bowlers go for a bit, try to get the shine off the ball. There is a lot that can go on in the Test matches in New Zealand. It is going to be an exciting series and one that we can't wait for."When asked why the India-New Zealand series has only two Tests, Santner pointed to New Zealand's history of playing shorter Test series as well as financial factors."For a long time, New Zealand played two-match series. There’s obviously the money side of it as well.""I know it costs a lot to play Test cricket. (It is about) timing as well; white-ball brings in the crowds in New Zealand, it brings the money. That's why I guess it is the 10-2 split."However, Santner said playing India, even in a two-Test series, remains a major opportunity for New Zealand."Whenever India come, even if it is only two Test matches, it is going to be exciting. Everyone wants to challenge themselves against the best in the world and they are up there. For us, it is going to be an important series like it is for India with the (World Test Championship) points that are on offer."
Article Summary: Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma will return to New Zealand for five ODIs, five T20Is and two Tests. New Zealand's first target will be to win the ODI series against India at home. The Blackcaps will then travel to England for World Cup preparations in September 2027.

Article Title: Why Pakistan captain Fatima Sana was penalised after Women's Asia Cup loss to India
Article Text:
Fatima Sana (Image credit: ACC)

Gesture after dismissing Shafali

Second offence in 24 months

Pakistan captain Fatima Sana has been fined 10 per cent of her match fee and given one demerit point for breaching the ICC Code of Conduct during the Women's Asia Cup match against India.Pakistan lost the Group A match by seven wickets at the Dubai International Stadium on Saturday.The International Cricket Council (ICC) said on Monday that Fatima had breached Article 2.5 of the Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel.The rule relates to ‘using language, actions or gestures which disparage, or which could provoke an aggressive reaction from a batter upon his/her dismissal during an International Match.’The incident took place on the final ball of the second over of India's chase of 56.Fatima dismissed India opener Shafali Verma through a caught-and-bowled dismissal. After taking the catch, the Pakistan captain gestured towards the pavilion.The gesture led to the Code of Conduct charge.This is Fatima's second offence within a 24-month period. Her latest demerit point takes her total to two.Her previous demerit point came during Pakistan's opening T20 International against Ireland in Dublin on August 6, 2025."Fatima admitted the offence and accepted the sanction proposed by Supriya Rani Das of the Emirates ICC International Panel of Match Referees, so there was no need for a formal hearing," further said the ICC.The charges were brought by on-field umpires Nimali Perera and Shathira Jakir Jesy, third umpire Rokeya Sultana and fourth umpire Rabab Ahsan.Level 1 breaches carry a minimum penalty of an official reprimand and a maximum penalty of 50 per cent of a player's match fee. Players can also receive one or two demerit points.Despite the penalty, Fatima will be available to lead Pakistan in their next Women's Asia Cup match against Hong Kong China on Tuesday.Pakistan need a win to reach the semi-finals.Seven-time champions India and defending champions Sri Lanka have already secured their places in the last four.
Article Summary: Fatima Sana fined 10 per cent of her match fee and given one demerit point for breaching the ICC Code of Conduct during the Women's Asia Cup match against India. The incident took place on the final ball of the second over of India's chase of 56. Pakistan lost the Group A match by seven wickets at the Dubai International Stadium.

NEW DELHI: Tripura chief minister Manik Saha has fulfilled a promise made to Commonwealth Games gold medallist Asmita Dey, with the state government allotting her a piece of land in Agartala to build a house.The 23-year-old judoka was honoured in Tripura on Wednesday after becoming the first Indian judoka to win a Commonwealth Games gold medal.Dey won the women’s -48kg title in Glasgow after defeating Canada’s Heidi Quach in a dramatic golden-score contest. The state government also presented her with a cheque of Rs 10 lakh as part of the felicitation.Speaking at the event, Saha highlighted Dey’s difficult journey from a small village in South Tripura to the top of the Commonwealth Games podium. Her father, he noted, worked as a cycle mechanic in Sonaichari.“The journey from an obscure village in South Tripura to a podium finish at Glasgow was a race against time. Her father was a cycle mechanic at Sonaichari. Against all odds, she stood firm on her mission and achieved phenomenal success for the country,” he said.The chief minister recalled meeting Dey at Tripura Bhavan in New Delhi after her return from the Games.During that meeting, the judoka had expressed her wish to have a house in Agartala.“During the meeting, Asmita revealed she desperately wanted a house in Agartala. I promised to fulfil her wish, and today a piece of land has been allotted to her,” he said.Saha said Dey’s achievement could motivate more young athletes from Tripura to pursue sport at the highest level. He also urged her to remain disciplined as she prepares for the Asian Games, particularly because of the strict anti-doping requirements.“I urge Asmita to remain alert, particularly about food, because she has to pass through a stringent dope test before joining the prestigious Asian Games. We believe she will shine again in the Asian Games by winning a medal for the country,” he said.Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Tinku Roy, Agartala Mayor Dipak Majumder and Arjuna award-winning gymnast Dipa Karmakar were among those who attended the felicitation ceremony.
Article Summary: Tripura chief minister Manik Saha has fulfilled a promise made to Commonwealth Games gold medallist Asmita Dey. The state government allotting her a piece of land in Agartala to build a house.
